correction.text: The principality as the 1468 Cliopatria shape draws it, from the year it separated from Georgia: 'In 1465 he defeated Georgian King George VIII at the battle near Paravani lake and separated from Georgia'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria begins the principality in 1468; the page dates the separation to 1465, and Cliopatria's Kingdom of Georgia row (127,772 km2 to 1462) resumes in 1468 as 27,616 km2, so 1463-1467 is a gap in both. The extent is the 1468 shape; the page gives no boundary.

42,721 km2. The page gives no area, so nothing to compare; its lead says the territory 'consisted of the modern-day Samtskhe-Javakheti region and the historical region of Tao-Klarjeti', which the shape (40.4-43.9 E, 39.7-41.7 N) covers. The page is silent on any border change between 1468 and 1501; Adjara came 'fully under Meskhetian rule' under Mzetchabuk (1500-1515) with no year, and the shape carries no visible change at that point.

42,624 km2, 97 km2 less than 1468-1501: a cartographic difference, as the page records no territorial event in 1502 (it dates Kaikhosro I's agreement to help Shah Ismail against the Aq Qoyunlu to no year; the Safavids appear as a Cliopatria neighbour from 1502).

correction.text: The 1502 shape carried forward: the principality under Mzetchabuki (to 1515), Manuchar I (1515-1518) and Qvarqvare III (1518-1535), per the article's reign table

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria drops the principality after 1506, but the page's reign table and narrative (1515 abdication, 1518 revolt, 1535 annexation) show it continuing to 1535. The page gives no boundary for these years; Adjara 'came fully under Meskhetian rule' in Mzetchabuk's reign and is assumed inside the shape.

Infobox 'Established: 1266' is the Georgian-era atabegate; Cliopatria starts the shape in 1468.

ledger.note: 1535: Rostom Gurieli takes Adjara and Lazeti from Samtskhe. The page says he received them after helping Bagrat III; the year is the invasion's, the regions are the page's, the Gurieli state being the principality of Guria by my reading.

region.text: Samtskhe, annexed after Qvarqvare III was captured at the Battle of Murjakheti near Akhalkalaki (Adjara and Lazeti already to Guria, ledger 1)

ledger.note: 1535: King Bagrat III, with Rostom Gurieli and Odishian allies, invades Samtskhe, captures Qvarqvare III and annexes the principality. 'Georgians had annexed Principality of Samtskhe.' The article links Bagrat to Bagrat III of Imereti. Was a dissolve; the principality returns in 1545 (ledger 3), so the state now only loses the land here (fx-46 R056).

minus.text: the principality as Cliopatria's 1502 shape draws it (Samtskhe-Javakheti and Tao-Klarjeti)

region.text: the principality's land (Cliopatria 1502 shape) without Adjara, which stays with Guria (ledger 1) until the Ottomans took it from Guria in 1582 (Childir Eyalet page)

ledger.note: 1545: Kaikhosro II, Qvarqvare III's youngest surviving son, asked the Ottomans to expel the Imeretian and Kartlian forces; Bagrat and Rostom were 'decisively defeated, in 1545, at Sokhoista' and 'Samtskhe became vassal of the Ottoman Empire'. The reign table gives Kaikhosro II 1545-1573. The principality is back on its 1502 shape (the page gives no boundary for 1545-1578; Peace of Amasya, 29 May 1555, left 'western Samtskhe' to the Ottomans and 'eastern Samtskhe' to the Safavids, undated on the ground, so the shape is one soft block). Overlord: Ottoman 1545-1555, then Safavid per the Childir Eyalet page ('a vassal state of Safavid dynasty'); recorded in hierarchy.csv by the orchestrator, not as vassal events here. Supersedes p1500-p1599 events/1 (Imereti loss to the Ottomans in 1545).

region.text: the principality's land, taken into the Ottoman province of Childir in 1578

ledger.note: 1578: 'when the new province was established, they appointed the former Georgian prince' Minuchir (later Mustafa Pasha) as first governor; the Ottomans 'took the Ahiska region from the Principality of Meskheti, a vassal state of Safavid dynasty'. The Samtskhe page puts the end of the Jaqeli principality at 1625 (infobox) or 1628 ('until 1628', then Childir Eyalet): that is the end of Jaqeli rule inside the Ottoman province (hereditary from 1625), not of an independent border, so the map ends the principality at the 1578 annexation (fx-46 R056). Not listed under identity.successors (fx-46 review): the compiler's succession rule R2 lets a listed successor win every conflict from its own start year (1299 for the Ottomans), and the Ottoman keyframes of 1507-1572 draw 167-169 of this principality's cells, which the size rule gave to Samtskhe until now (conflicts.csv: 1,026 cell-years, 1507-1534); as a successor the Ottomans would take the principality at their 1507/1516 snaps. The cells left at the end of 1578 fall to nobody and the Ottoman 1579 keyframe takes them in 1579.

wars.name: Qvarqvare II's rebellion against George VIII
wars.outcome: Samtskhe separated from Georgia after Qvarqvare II's victory at Lake Paravani (1465); he had called in Uzun Hasan of the Aq Qoyunlu against the Georgian king in 1462.
wars.note: 'In 1462 Qvarqvare II Jaqeli called against the king of Georgia' (Uzun Hasan). No zone is contested: the page names no ground taken or held in 1462-1464.

wars.name: Aq Qoyunlu and Ottoman pressure on Samtskhe
wars.outcome: The page records the attacks without a territorial result: 'The Aq Qoyunlu launched major attacks in 1466, 1476-1477 and 1485 and from 1479 the Ottoman Empire started to encroach on the territories.' In 1479 Qvarqvare II ravaged the land around Erzurum, 'reducing the city to tributary status'.
wars.note: Erzurum is not drawn as a vassal: the page gives no end to the tribute, so the pair of vassal events the validator requires cannot be written honestly.

wars.name: Bagrat III's invasion of Samtskhe
wars.outcome: Qvarqvare III captured at Murjakheti; Samtskhe annexed, Rostom Gurieli given Adjara and Lazeti.
wars.note: The Ottoman riposte (Karagak 1543, Sokhoista 1545) belongs to the restored principality, outside this dossier's life.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is given by the page; the frontiers with Kartli, Imereti, Guria and the Aq Qoyunlu and Ottoman lands are approximate.

1536-1544 the land is Imereti's after the annexation (no extent drawn here); from 1545 no page gives a boundary for the restored principality, so the 1502 shape is carried forward and the Amasya split (west Ottoman, east Safavid, 1555) is not drawn.

notes:
Scope: the dossier covers 1465-1535, the principality's independent life from the page's dated separation to the annexation. Cliopatria's two shapes (1468-1506) cover only part of it: two new keyframes extend the same core back to 1465 and forward to 1534. The principality was restored in 1545 as an Ottoman vassal (Kaikhosro II 1545-1573 per the reign table) and the page's infobox runs to 'Disestablished: 1625' (the text says its rulers reigned 'until 1628'); the Childir Eyalet page dates the Ottoman province to 1578 and calls Samtskhe 'a vassal state of Safavid dynasty' just before that. Those years (1545-1625) are not drawn here: the pages opened give no boundary for them and the page budget was 1-2 pages. A gap-filler or the Ottoman group (me-10) should decide whether to add a second life (1545-1578) as an Ottoman vassal.
Disagreements: infobox 'Established: 1266' / 'Disestablished: 1625' versus Cliopatria 1468-1506 and the text's 1465 and 1535. The 1465 start follows the text. Bagrat III is identified as the king of Imereti only through the article's link; the Imereti dossier (eu-19) should carry the matching gain in 1535. Adjara/Lazeti go to Guria (Rostom Gurieli) in 1535 by the article; the Guria dossier should carry the matching gain.
Region names: 'Adjara' is a gazetteer region. 'Tao-Klarjeti' is not in the gazetteer (listed in the report as gazetteer_names_needed); the dossier's shapes use the Cliopatria shape instead.
Counterparts: Ottoman Empire and Aq Qoyunlu have dossiers elsewhere (me-10, me-09).
fx-46 R056 (3 Nov 2026): the life now runs 1465-1535 and 1545-1578. 1535: Samtskhe annexed by Bagrat III (land to Imereti, ledger 2); 1545: Sokhoista, principality restored as an Ottoman vassal (gain from Imereti, ledger 3, and keyframe 1545); 1578: Ottoman province of Childir (dissolve, counterpart ottoman-empire, ledger 4; not a listed successor, see ledger 4). The Samtskhe page's own end (1625 infobox, 1628 text) is the end of the Jaqeli dynasty's rule inside the Ottoman province, not drawn.
